quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated results: revenue rose 0.9% and core operating income (business profit) fell 0.6%. Operating income fell 23.7%, mainly on an impairment loss recorded on the battery separator film business of a Korean subsidiary; net income attributable to owners of the parent rose 2.1%.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 25,851 hundred million (FY2025: 25,633); core operating income JPY 1,419 hundred million (FY2025: 1,428); operating income JPY 972 hundred million (FY2025: 1,275); net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 795 hundred million (FY2025: 779)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 segment results: revenue rose in Fibers & Textiles, Carbon Fiber Composite Materials and Environment & Engineering and fell in Performance Chemicals and Life Science. Core operating income bridge (management analysis, JPY hundred million): volume +258 (higher sales volumes mainly in Carbon Fiber Composite Materials on recovering aerospace demand, and in Environment & Engineering on reverse osmosis membranes for the Middle East), price -22 (strategic pricing progressed, but price competition intensified in Carbon Fiber Composite Materials), cost and other -235 (higher costs with higher utilisation), FX translation -9.
quarterly_data.figure: Segment revenue / core operating income (JPY hundred million): Fibers & Textiles 10,511 / 680; Performance Chemicals 8,944 / 563; Carbon Fiber Composite Materials 3,001 / 176; Environment & Engineering 2,669 / 288; Life Science 524 / -1; Other 202 / 25

quarterly_data.signal: Performance Chemicals segment FY2026 (management analysis): in the film business demand grew for electronic-component-related and automotive capacitor applications, but battery separator film sales were sluggish. In electronic & information materials, sales of new products for power inductors grew, while OLED-related and circuit materials were hit by weak panel demand and intensified competition in China. Resins were held back by a weak automotive market and chemicals by market deterioration. Segment revenue fell 5.3% and core operating income fell 6.2%.
quarterly_data.figure: Performance Chemicals revenue JPY 8,944 hundred million (-5.3%); core operating income JPY 563 hundred million (-6.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Carbon Fiber Composite Materials FY2026 (management analysis): aerospace applications recovered steadily, but general industrial applications such as pressure vessels entered an adjustment phase and wind turbine blade demand was slow to recover; revenue was flat and core operating income fell 21.7%. Under IGNITION 2028 management expects Boeing 787 production rates to recover and space and defence demand to grow, and over the medium to long term sees wind blades, fuel-cell vehicle hydrogen tanks and electrode substrates, and UAM as new opportunities.
quarterly_data.figure: Carbon Fiber Composite Materials revenue JPY 3,001 hundred million (flat); core operating income JPY 176 hundred million (-21.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: New medium-term management plan IGNITION 2028 covers the company's fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028 (April 2026 to March 2029; FY2027 to FY2029 in fiscal-year-end terms). Targets for its final year (the company's fiscal 2028, FY2029): revenue JPY 30,000 hundred million, core operating income JPY 2,300 hundred million, core operating income margin 8%, ROIC about 7%, ROE about 8%, D/E ratio 0.7 or below (guideline), versus FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) actuals of JPY 25,851 hundred million, JPY 1,419 hundred million, 5.5%, ROIC 4.7% and ROE 4.5%; assumptions JPY 150 per US dollar and crude oil US$72.5 per barrel. The long-term policy TORAY Challenges 2035 targets ROIC of 10% in 2035.
quarterly_data.figure: IGNITION 2028 final-year targets: revenue JPY 30,000 hundred million; core operating income JPY 2,300 hundred million; margin 8%; ROIC about 7%; ROE about 8%

quarterly_data.signal: Previous plan Project AP-G 2025 (the company's fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025, i.e. FY2024 to FY2026) outcome: revenue and core operating income missed the final-year (FY2026) targets, mainly on volume shortfalls, which management attributes to intensified competition from the rise of Chinese competitors, accelerating protectionism and rapid inflation; free cash flow and the D/E ratio met their targets. By segment, Fibers & Textiles and Environment & Engineering met their core operating income targets, while Performance Chemicals (target 910 vs actual 563), Carbon Fiber Composite Materials (360 vs 176) and Life Science missed (JPY hundred million).
quarterly_data.figure: Final-year target vs actual: revenue JPY 28,000 vs 25,851 hundred million; core operating income JPY 1,800 vs 1,419 hundred million; core operating income margin 6% vs 5.5%

quarterly_data.signal: IGNITION 2028 strategy for films and electronic & information materials (management): it expects in-vehicle film demand to expand with more xEVs, automation and connectivity, electronic components to become more advanced on rising AI demand, and power demand to grow; functional films are positioned as the core of the film growth strategy, differentiating films for release applications (functional-film manufacturing processes and protection) and for film capacitors through thinner gauges and higher cleanliness. In semiconductors it expects memory and logic to increase greatly on data-center growth driven by generative AI and power semiconductors to grow with xEVs and renewables, and aims to keep and expand high shares in semiconductor, electronic component and display applications while accelerating new businesses such as next-generation semiconductor and optical communication materials.

FY2026 capital expenditure (including right-of-use and intangible assets) fell 32.0%: Fibers & Textiles 317 (maintenance and renewal), Performance Chemicals 527 (including the polypropylene film production capacity expansion at Toray's Nasu Plant), Carbon Fiber Composite Materials 453 (including the carbon fiber capacity expansion at Toray Composite Materials America), Environment & Engineering 91, Life Science 30 (JPY hundred million).

Planned new facilities for the next fiscal year (FY2027; plan as of March 31, 2026, under the new segments that merge water treatment and pharmaceuticals & medical into Water Treatment & Healthcare and move engineering into Other): Performance Chemicals JPY 67,000 million, mainly the polypropylene film production capacity expansion at Toray's Nasu Plant; Carbon Fiber Composite Materials JPY 35,000 million for carbon fiber capacity expansions at Toray Composite Materials America, Toray Advanced Materials Korea and Toray Carbon Fibers Europe; Fibers & Textiles JPY 39,000 million including a new sewn-products facility at Toray MAS Apparel India; Water Treatment & Healthcare JPY 11,000 million; Other JPY 6,000 million; Corporate JPY 2,000 million. No retirement of facilities with a material effect on capacity is planned.
quarterly_data.figure: Planned capex JPY 160,000 million in total; Performance Chemicals JPY 67,000 million (Nasu polypropylene film expansion)

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: Toray developed a new semiconductor back-end material needed to make ultra-thin chips of 30 um or less, for AI semiconductors and power semiconductors for xEVs and industrial equipment: a temporary bonding material for the back-grinding process using high-modulus polyimide that combines thinness and thickness uniformity, PFAS-free and NMP-free. The company will build a mass-production system and aims for mass production by 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: chips 30 um or less; mass production targeted by 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Other FY2026 R&D results: a recycling technology that decomposes thermoset CFRP while keeping carbon fiber strength and surface quality, and a carbon fiber nonwoven from the recycled fiber (CO2 expected to be cut by 50% or more versus virgin fiber); a nanofiltration membrane element scaled to practical size that recovers lithium from used lithium-ion batteries at 95% or more yield; launch of a separation membrane module for biopharmaceutical purification with 4x or more the filtration performance of conventional products; and a piezoelectric polymer working at 200 C or above, targeted for practical use around 2028. Group R&D expense by segment: Fibers & Textiles about 10%, Performance Chemicals about 26%, Carbon Fiber Composite Materials about 16%, Environment & Engineering about 7%, Life Science about 3%, corporate R&D about 38%.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expense JPY 759 hundred million (parent JPY 536 hundred million)

quarterly_data.signal: Material contract: Toray Composite Materials America has a carbon fiber composite materials supply contract with Boeing running from September 30, 2015 to December 31, 2028.

Portfolio changes (material contracts section): during FY2026 Toray sold all its interests in the battery separator film joint venture LG Toray Hungary Battery Separator Kft. (with LG Chem) and in Japan Vilene (with Freudenberg), and on February 5, 2026 entered a joint venture contract with Metawater for Suido Kiko (water treatment equipment). On May 29, 2026 it signed an agreement to sell its entire 66% stake in Soda Aromatic (a Performance Chemicals subsidiary), together with Mitsui & Co.'s 34%, to a subsidiary set up by Korea's Samyang Corporation.
